Based on my search, here's information about the **Navy P-3** (Lockheed P-3 Orion), a maritime patrol aircraft that has been a cornerstone of naval aviation for decades:

## Overview

The **P-3 Orion** is a four-engine, low-wing maritime patrol aircraft developed by Lockheed. Originally designed for anti-submarine warfare (ASW), it has served extensively with the U.S. Navy and numerous allied nations. The aircraft is in the 135,000-pound gross weight class and is powered by four T56 turboprop engines.

## Key Specifications

| Feature | Specification |
|---------|-------------|
| **Engines** | 4 × Allison T56-A-14 turboprops |
| **Gross Weight** | ~135,000 lbs |
| **Maximum Speed** | 405 KIAS (test envelope); operational limit ~300 KIAS sustained |
| **Service Ceiling** | 35,000 ft (clearance limit); 25,000 ft (test envelope) |
| **Crew** | Typically 8+ (pilot, co-pilot, tactical coordinator, navigator/communicator, sensor operators) |
| **Science/Mission Crew** | Up to 18 personnel + 6 air crew (NASA configuration) |

## Primary Missions

The P-3 Orion was designed as a **submarine hunter** to succeed the flying boats of World War II. Its core missions include:

- **Anti-Submarine Warfare (ASW)** – Using sonobuoys, magnetic anomaly detection (MAD), and acoustic sensors
- **Maritime Patrol & Surveillance** – Extended patrols over ocean areas
- **Search and Rescue (SAR)** – Long-endurance search operations
- **Anti-Surface Warfare** – Capable of carrying missiles, mines, and torpedoes
- **Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance (ISR)** – Electronic support measures (ESM) and radar

## Combat Systems & Sensors

The P-3 features an extensive sensor suite:
- **Radar systems** for surface and air search
- **ESM (Electronic Support Measures)** for electronic intelligence
- **MAD (Magnetic Anomaly Detection)** boom for detecting submerged submarines
- **Acoustic sensor stations** for analyzing sonobuoy data
- **Infrared and optical systems**

## Global Operators & Current Status

The P-3 has been operated by numerous navies and air forces worldwide, including:
- **U.S. Navy** (being phased out in favor of the P-8 Poseidon)
- **Hellenic Navy** (Greece) – Mixed navy/air force crews
- **Argentine Navy** – Currently modernizing fleet with P-3C acquisitions from Norway (2024-2026)
- **Royal New Zealand Air Force** – Historical operator

## Legacy

As retired Rear Admiral James "Poopie" Schear stated: *"I think they helped win the Cold War."* The P-3 Orion community has a special appreciation for the aircraft's accomplishments in decades of maritime patrol and anti-submarine operations.

The P-3 is gradually being replaced by the **P-8 Poseidon** in U.S. Navy service, but continues to serve in various capacities worldwide.

Sources:
1. https://airbornescience.nasa.gov/sites/default/files/P-3B%20Experimenter%20Handbook%20548-HDBK-0001.pdf
2. https://www.navalanalyses.com/2018/05/greek-maritime-patrol-aircraft-past.html
3. https://en.yna.co.kr/view/AEN20230518003900325
4. https://www.zona-militar.com/en/2026/03/02/the-argentine-navy-moves-forward-with-the-incorporation-of-its-third-p-3c-orion-aircraft-following-a-new-payment-to-norway/
5. https://airandspace.si.edu/air-and-space-quarterly/issue-13/orion-p3
6. https://www.defenceconnect.com.au/naval/7444-hmnzs-te-kaha-arrives-in-new-zealand-following-capability-upgrade
7. https://web.uri.edu/rotc/meet/john-h-thompson-jr/
